items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: Glenn Miller was recording, and Glenn gave me two numbers to make up for... I made up... Wham... Glenn Miller told the manager, just give him a check when he comes, we'll get him out of arranging... I'd rehearse it... I rehearsed In The Mood

ctx.x: And that's why any white musician can sit down and play in Glenn Miller's band or someplace else. But the black musicians can get eight or ten different tones on his horn, so when he gets in a band, that's why it's hard for him to fit.
Well, now, the different tones, this had nothing to do with the vibrato, really.

items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: Metro-Goldwyn-Meyer, he's got the -- Glen Miller (unintelligible) -- oh, I was doing around about 10,000 a year in royalties.

ctx.x: Well, what sort of royalties did you get from the -- from records?

I never was paid too well, only bread (inaudible) paid pretty well. Like maybe a couple of thousand a year and Metro-Goldwyn-Meyer, he's got the -- Glen Miller (unintelligible) -- oh, I was doing around about 10,000 a year in royalties. that was good.
Well, I mean, the thing I never understand is when you get those lists of royalties on records
